pages.text:
About Halimbawa
A short history of the town, and its vision and mission.
History
Halimbawa began as a fishing village at the mouth of the Ilog Halimbawa. It became a municipality in **1950** and today has 12 barangays and about 38,000 residents.

All of this is invented for testing.

Milestones

Founded as a municipality Separated from its neighbouring town.
New municipal hall Built on the town plaza.
Business One-Stop Shop opens Permits in one visit.
Vision
A safe, clean and prosperous Halimbawa where every resident is served well.

pages.description: How to apply for or renew a business permit, what to bring, and the fees.
pages.text:
Business permit
How to apply for or renew a business permit, what to bring, and the fees.
How to apply

Fill in the unified form Get it at the Business One-Stop Shop or download it.
Submit your requirements Bring the documents listed below.
Pay and claim your permit Pay at the Treasurer's Office window 3. Most permits are released the same day.
What to bring

Barangay business clearance 
DTI, SEC or CDA registration 
Contract of lease or proof of ownership of the place of business 
Community Tax Certificate 
Fees
| Business | Fee |
|---|---|
| Sari-sari store | ₱500 |
| Restaurant | ₱1,500 |
| Other | Assessed at the window |

Questions

When must I renew? On or before January 20 of each year.
Can I apply online? Not yet. The form can be downloaded, but submission is in person.

pages.title: Town-wide flood drill on November 5
pages.description: All 12 barangays take part in a flood evacuation drill.
pages.text:
Town-wide flood drill on November 5
All 12 barangays take part in a flood evacuation drill.

The Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office will hold a flood evacuation drill in all 12 barangays on **November 5, 2026**, starting at 9:00 AM. Sirens will sound for one minute.

Residents near the river should follow their barangay's evacuation route.
